root_idea.summary: The root centers on the upper arm, and by extension on strength, support, and assistance; it also has a distinct lexical branch for cutting or lopping.
root_idea.development: The bodily sense of the upper arm develops figuratively into support, a helper, or a source of strength, and further into sides or supporting structural parts. A separate branch denotes cutting trees and related tools or products.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun is displayed under the normalized classical citation form عَضُد.

senses.definition: The upper arm, between the elbow and the shoulder.
senses.usage_conditions: The bodily sense; the Quranic forms are inflected as عَضُدًا and عَضُدَكَ.

senses.definition: Support, aid, or a source of strength; figuratively, an aider or assistant.
senses.usage_conditions: Used metaphorically of a person or group that strengthens or assists another, including the construction “to strengthen one’s support by” someone. In the Quran, the singular may represent supporting helpers collectively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hit or hurt someone’s upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb governing a person as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid or assist someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative use of the verb derived from the arm as a means of strength; distinct from the bodily action of striking the arm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a male camel: to seize a female camel by the upper arm and throw her down for mating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized camel-related use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind or attach a thong, amulet, or similar object upon the upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is attached to the عَضُد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To walk alongside a beast, keeping to its right or left side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of accompanying a riding or working animal without leaving its side.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach riding camels or other beasts from the surrounding tracts and gather them together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The gathering is performed from the sides or surrounding areas of the animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or lop trees, including cutting off foliage or branches for animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action may be performed with a مِعْضَد or similar cutting implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a saddle: to gall or wound a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The saddle or its fitting is the agent of the injury.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer an ailment in the upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive or stative bodily construction, also extended in the source to analogous complaints in other body parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel: to suffer the disease called عَضَدٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The disease is described in the lexical evidence chiefly in connection with camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of rain moisture: to reach or penetrate to the measure of the upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV usage describing the depth reached by moisture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an arrow or other missile: to go to the right or left of the target or butt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV use describing a shot that veers aside or falls beside the mark.

other_classical_meanings.definition: They aided or assisted one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put or place a thing upon or under one’s upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is synonymous with placing or holding something under the arm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become strong or to strengthen oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form VIII use derived from the arm as a means of strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask, seek, or desire aid or assistance from someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The person sought is construed with بِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gather fruit by cutting it off from a tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action includes both severing the fruit and collecting it for eating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom about fatness, the upper arm may stand for the whole body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is based on the upper arm’s fatness being taken as an indication of general bodily fatness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A side, lateral part, adjacent quarter, or surrounding tract.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to the side of an armpit, road, house, object, or region, and to the tracts surrounding riding animals; it can also denote the direction from which wind blows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A raised side, enclosing border, or retaining structure around a tank, watering-trough, road, or irrigated plot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often used of the stones or ridges that confine water or mark the sides of a built or cultivated area.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A row of palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use, also reported for a row situated along a watercourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two branches or attachments of a sandal strap that lie over the foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the dual for the paired sandal parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two wooden side pieces attached to the front part of a camel saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized saddle-making term for paired structural pieces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Afflicted with a complaint or ailment of the upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of a person or animal; the lexical evidence also applies it to a camel with the disease عَضَدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel: afflicted with the disease called عَضَدٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival specialization of the camel-disease terminology.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who has drawn near to the two sides of a watering-trough or tank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive use based on approaching the sides of the watering place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A male wild ass that gathers the she-asses from their different quarters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological description of the animal’s gathering behavior.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a short upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or an arm whose portion between elbow and shoulder is short.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Short, compact, and moderately proportioned in build, especially with thick or short upper arms.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of women, men, and young men; the source varies the associated forms by gender and usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel: one that stays apart and does not approach the watering-trough until it is unoccupied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a camel that separates itself from the herd at the watering place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A crosswise hot-iron brand placed on a camel’s upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the mark itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One of a pair of side pieces or posts of a door, buckle, bit, or yoke.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for paired structural parts positioned on the right and left or at the sides of the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A close attendant or constant companion who does not leave another’s side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use derived from the idea of a supporting side piece or close adjacency.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Large in the upper arms.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of a person’s physical build.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a male camel: one that seizes a female camel by the upper arm and makes her lie down for mating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial form of the specialized camel usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who walks alongside a beast on its right or left.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial description of an animal attendant or driver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow that falls to the right or left of the target or butt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use for a shot that misses laterally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Two rows of palm trees growing along the sides of a river or rivulet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The dual denotes the two bordering rows; the plural may denote palms growing along watercourse sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cutter or lopper of trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial noun for a person who cuts or lops trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slender in the upper arm, or having one upper arm shorter than the other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical descriptor of asymmetry or lack of flesh in the upper arm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An amulet, armlet, or bracelet worn or bound upon the upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same implement may be described as a thong-bound amulet or as an ornamental armlet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A heavy cutting implement, reaping-hook-like tool, or sword used for cutting trees; also a sword used to cut bones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The tool may draw down branches for animals or be a sword employed for lopping and cutting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A money purse worn or bound upon the upper arm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traveller’s arm-bound purse for carrying spending money.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment decorated with figured work, embroidery, or stripes at the sides or around the upper-arm area.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptive use concerns the placement or form of the garment’s ornamentation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels: branded on the upper arms with the mark called عِضَاد.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of animals bearing the specified brand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firmly made or solidly built.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as an epithet describing a person’s physical constitution; the transmitted wording is noted as variant in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of dates beginning to ripen: ripening on one side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of uneven or one-sided ripening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular herb or leguminous plant with a yellow blossom and bitter or viscous qualities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare plant name, with variant descriptions of whether it is classed among herbs or small trees.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Cutting or scattering foliage is covered by the broader tree-cutting meaning.
Pointer-only continuation naming a cross-referenced form.
Cut or lopped tree material and fallen foliage are covered by the tree-cutting branch.
Buckle sides are covered by the broader paired-side-pieces meaning.
Bit sides are covered by the broader paired-side-pieces meaning.
Yoke pieces are covered by the broader paired-side-pieces meaning.

cautions: The public headword is normalized to عَضُد, while the Quran occurrences are inflected forms عَضُدًا and عَضُدَكَ.
The support sense is metaphorical and construction-sensitive; the bodily sense remains separately represented.
